name: Andrew Hallam
intro: I study how complex quantum systems evolve, how they store information, and how we can understand them using tensor networks.
about: I am a Quantum Fellow at EPCC, University of Edinburgh. My research connects quantum many-body physics, tensor networks, and quantum information, with a particular interest in dynamics beyond thermal equilibrium.

I use numerical and analytical approaches to explore quantum chaos, many-body scars, and the structure of entanglement. My work also investigates quantum resources for computation and spin-chain models of curved spacetime.
Previously, I held postdoctoral positions at the University of Leeds and Ghent University. I completed my PhD in Physics at University College London, supervised by Andrew Green.

themes.title: Tensor networks
themes.short: Finding tractable descriptions of entanglement and complex quantum states.
themes.description: Tensor networks turn the entanglement structure of a quantum state into a practical description. I develop and use matrix product states and related methods to study quantum dynamics, path integrals, and the limits of classical simulation.
themes.detail: My work includes path integrals over matrix product states, the relationship between multiscale entanglement renormalization and matrix product operators, and effective descriptions of many-body dynamics.

themes.title: Quantum dynamics & chaos
themes.short: Understanding thermalisation, many-body scars, and persistent quantum coherence.
themes.description: How does an isolated quantum system approach equilibrium, and when does that process fail? I investigate the connection between classical chaos and quantum thermalisation, along with the special trajectories and states that support long-lived coherent motion.
themes.detail: Research directions include quantum many-body scars, semiclassical periodic orbits, time crystals, and methods for identifying coherent dynamics within otherwise complex many-body systems.

themes.title: Quantum information
themes.short: Connecting many-body physics with the resources needed for quantum computation.
themes.description: Entanglement is only one part of the information structure of quantum matter. I study nonstabilizerness, often called quantum magic, and its relationship to criticality, dynamics, and the difficulty of simulating quantum systems.
themes.detail: I have also worked on hierarchical quantum classifiers and tensor-network descriptions of neural networks, exploring connections between quantum information and machine learning.

themes.title: Analogue gravity
themes.short: Exploring effective black-hole geometries in interacting spin chains.
themes.description: Models that can be studied in condensed matter and on quantum processors can also provide a setting for questions inspired by curved spacetime. I investigate chiral spin chains with effective event horizons and black-hole geometries.
themes.detail: This work connects microscopic spin models with scrambling, apparent thermality, and quantum information in simulated black holes.

education.detail: Tensor network descriptions of quantum entanglement in path integrals, thermalisation and machine learning. Supervisor: Andrew Green.
Distinction. Research on tensor-network descriptions of out-of-equilibrium quantum systems.

teaching: Taught parts of PHYS3003: Advanced Techniques in Theoretical Physics and PHYS5017M: Quantum Many-Body Physics at the University of Leeds.
Supervised year-long Master’s research projects at Ghent University and the University of Leeds, and co-supervised PhD students at Leeds.
Received the University of Leeds Mentorship Award for Engineering and Physical Sciences in 2025.
service: Organised the University of Leeds internal quantum theory seminar and the Leeds–Loughborough–Nottingham non-equilibrium seminar.
Helped organise QCumber at UCL in 2015 and 2016 and the 24th Symposium on Quantum Matter and High-Energy Physics in 2022.
Helped deliver a hands-on quantum computing workshop for Year 12 and 13 students through the University of Leeds Reach for Excellence programme.
